chapter: Hampton, Blue Note and the electric guitar
title: Recording with Lionel Hampton: "Charlie Was a Sailor"
summary: They listen to the Victor session with Lionel Hampton, made out west around 1940 on a tour with a four-piece combo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I'd like to play another song, some Lionel Hampton stuff. Hold on just a second.
This is the Lionel Hampton recording, "Charlie Was A Sailor".
I think it might be Lionel singing. But I don't know who the piano player is. The piano player's real good. (Marlowe Morris - ed.)
Yeah. You played an electric on this session, huh?
This was one of the first --
-- records you made with an electric, I think.
That was made out here. (Note: Rust's "Jazz Records" claims New York-ed.)
When you first came out here? SING'S "funky butt, funky butt, funky butt."
Yeah. A Leo, boy, God bless his soul.
You can certainly tell whose session this is.
It's good, though. It's good. Did you work with him for awhile?
Yeah. Out this way and back east.
Oh, it was a kind of a national tour with Lionel?
